result.summary: The page mostly looks intact, but there are a few visual problems: the promotional banner has severely low-contrast white text on a pale mint background, a restaurant name is truncated without an ellipsis, and a category chip is clipped awkwardly at the screen edge.

issues.description: The promo banner text ('3 free deliveries for you' and 'Use code TALLINN3 at checkout · min. order €10') is white/very light on a pale mint-green background, making it nearly unreadable and failing contrast requirements.
issues.suggestion: Use a dark text color (e.g., dark green or near-black) on the light banner, or darken the banner background so white text meets WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1).

issues.description: The third restaurant card title in 'Fastest near you' shows 'Trattoria Piccol' — the name is cut off at the screen edge without an ellipsis, appearing broken rather than intentionally truncated.
issues.suggestion: Apply text truncation with an ellipsis within the card width, or ensure the card title wraps/clips within the visible card boundary instead of the viewport edge.

issues.description: A category filter chip after 'Healthy' is clipped at the right edge showing only a thin sliver, which looks like a rendering glitch rather than an obvious scrollable carousel.
issues.suggestion: Adjust chip spacing so a partially visible chip shows enough content (e.g., 30–50% visible) to signal horizontal scrollability, or add a subtle edge fade gradient.

issues.description: The 'Order now' button on the promo banner is white-on-light-green with light green text, giving it weak visual affordance against the already pale banner.
issues.suggestion: Increase the button's contrast (e.g., solid dark green button with white label) so the primary CTA stands out from the banner background.
